deal_stage: Technical kick-off completed, awaiting CFO budget validation
pitch_summary: Multi-agent Gen AI platform to automate vehicle return inspections (damage assessment, checklist reading, and charge calculation) across more than 700 physical branches, reducing manual inspection time and variability between assessors.
proposed_solution: Agentic pipeline on Azure combining computer-vision agents (damage image analysis) and text agents (checklist, billing policy, exceptions). 18-week implementation, US$510k in Year 1 (license + services).

ceo: Bruno Lasansky is CEO of Localiza, an Argentine industrial engineer educated at the Instituto Tecnológico de Buenos Aires, with an MBA from Wharton

Before taking the role, he was a partner at Bain & Company; he joined Localiza seven years ago, moved through Executive Director of Rental and then COO before becoming CEO — the first non-founder executive to lead the company in its 48-plus years of history
Under his leadership, Localiza operates a fleet of more than 630,000 vehicles and 700 physical branches across seven countries (Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Paraguay, Ecuador, Colombia, and Mexico)
Completed the merger with Unidas (Locamerica) in 2022 — one of the most complex antitrust deals in the country — and doubled technology investment since the start of the pandemic
In a public interview, he stated that the company's priority for the next cycle is return on invested capital (ROIC) combined with advancing generative AI adoption

Given this track record of post-merger operational standardization and an explicit priority on generative AI, Lasansky tends to evaluate automation proposals through the lens of 'does this improve fleet ROIC and scale consistently across our 700 branches, in the seven countries where we operate?'
